messages:
maya: Quick thread with the profiling dump from last night's L4/T4 sweep. Seeing a weird latency cliff around seqlen 512->768 that looks like a kernel selection flip + KV eviction thrash. Attaching the core snippets below.

jordan: yup saw alerts. p95 on the L4 pool spiked ~3x for some workloads. did we change any heuristics?

liam: Not intentionally. The new kernel-compat rule added last week will prefer the fused-attn path if workspace estimate < 1.2GB, otherwise it picks the fallback that keeps memory but is slower on small batches. That boundary might be wrong for L4 memory fragmentation.

maya: dump (trimmed):
```
# perf summary (trimmed)
model: rw-large
device: L4
batch: dynamic
seqlen: 384 -> p95 28ms
seqlen: 512 -> p95 34ms
seqlen: 640 -> p95 140ms  <-- regression
seqlen: 768 -> p95 150ms
seqlen: 1024 -> p95 120ms (uses packed-kv fallback)
kv-evict-count: increased by 4x at 640
kernel-picked: fast-fuse for <=600, fallback-gemm for >600
```

maya: interestingly, on A100/H100 the p95 stays flat across same seqlens (40-50ms). So it's very device-specific.

harper: hmm that suggests the kernel that triggers at ~640 is fine on H100 (large SMs), but on L4 the implementation ends up thrashing because of smaller scratch and different shared-mem rules. Could be workspace estimate mismatch + allocator fragmentation.

liam: i reproduced locally on a T4 VM. When the runtime switches to `fallback-gemm` the per-token kernel latency jumps, but more importantly the KV cache eviction rate spikes because the fallback's KV layout uses larger per-layer strides and forces early eviction under our default KV-reserve policy.

maya: reproduction script (short):
```
# run repro
python repro_profile.py --model rw-large --device l4 --batch 8 --seqlens 384,512,640,768,1024 --collect
# output -> /tmp/repro-197600
```

jordan: thanks. So two levers to consider: 1) tweak the seqlen branching threshold that picks fused vs fallback kernels for small-GPU devices, 2) adjust KV-reserve/eviction policy for devices with <= X GB to avoid thrash.

sanjay: propose new preset approach: device-family-aware seqlen-brackets + conservative kv-reserve for low-memory cards. Example (pseudo):
```
presets:
  l4-family:
    seqlen_brackets:
      - max: 512
        kernel: fast-fuse
      - max: 768
        kernel: small-gemm-optimized
      - max: inf
        kernel: packed-kv-fallback
    kv_reserve: 0.25  # keep 25% headroom to reduce eviction
    alloc_strategy: buddy-defrag
  a100-family:
    seqlen_brackets:
      - max: 1024
        kernel: fast-fuse
      - max: inf
        kernel: packed-kv-fallback
    kv_reserve: 0.07
```

harper: I like family presets. One nuance: some L4 variants have different SRAM behavior depending on driver. We should prefer a runtime probe that measures a cheap microbenchmark (tiny fused-attn run) to compute an empirical workspace factor rather than rely on static estimates.

liam: +1 for probe. We can add a boot-time quick-check: run a single-layer fused-attn with seq=640, bs=1 and compare runtime vs predicted; if error > 15% we bias the threshold toward the slower kernel. Cheap and robust.

maya: also noticed that small-batch workloads (batch <=4) on L4 behave differently — continuous batching heuristics were merging requests into a batch that crosses the seqlen threshold and then gets a bad kernel pick. Suggest we add batch-aware bracketing: bracket decisions should consider expected batching window (avg batch size) not just worst-case.

jordan: Agree. Proposed quick changes for the release branch:
- add device-family presets (l4/t4/a10) with conservative kv_reserve defaults
- implement probe-based workspace bias on startup
- make seqlen brackets consider avg_batch_size when evaluating kernel choices
- increase KV soft-reserve on low-memory devices to 20-30%

maya: putting a mini RFC in prod-ops PR tonight. Will include a reproducible perf table and the probe microbenchmark.

liam: small notes for patch: watch out for fallback semantics: the packed-kv-fallback changes layouts and isn't ABI-compatible with the fast path cache. When switching kernels mid-session we must clear per-request KV shims or risk double-lookup. We should prefer sticky kernel choice per model instance until a safe drain.

harper: good catch. add sticky-kernel: true for family presets as a conservative default. That avoids the flip-flop seen in the logs.

sanjay: automation question — do we add a daily job that runs these probes across our fleet and surfaces anomalies? could detect driver/firmware regressions.

jordan: yes, add to infra health checks. dev-bot: can you create a ticket? :robot_face:

dev-bot: created ISSUE-3821: "probe-based kernel bias + device-family presets for small-GPUs" assigned to @maya, @liam. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/ISSUE-3821

maya: thanks. Next steps: I will draft the preset YAML + probe script and post a small canary rollout plan (10% L4 pool then 100%). Target ship: 48h if no regressions.

jordan: sounds good. Also add a perf dashboard tile that overlays device-family p95 vs seqlen so we have continuous visibility.

maya: will do. If anyone wants to pair on the probe or the baseline numbers ping me. :thumbsup:
